newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S COMPAGNONI LEADS GIANT SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S COMPAGNONI LEADS GIANT SLALOM.

text.p: Italy's Deborah Compagnoni led after the first leg of the season's opening Alpine skiing World Cup giant slalom, raced in heavy snowfall on Saturday.
Olympic and world champion Compagnoni stormed out of the start house at 3,040 metres altitude to clock a fastest run time of one minute 04.59 seconds on the Rettenback piste.
Germany's overall World Cup holder Katja Seizinger was second quickest, 0.14 seconds behind, with Switzerland's Karin Roten third in 1:05.31.

Bad weather conditions and poor visibility due to heavy fog caused a number of short delays between decents and claimed a number of victims including Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg and Sabina Panzanini of Italy.
